hook: Why is her gold quote different?

editorial_brief.viewer_question: Why can the jeweller quote and gold price on my phone disagree?
editorial_brief.misconception: A gold price shown anywhere must be the same price a jeweller uses.
editorial_brief.mechanism: The phone may show a global dollar benchmark, MCX is a rupee futures contract, and a jeweller quote adds purity and retail components.
editorial_brief.proof_plan: The companion carousel will label a dated global benchmark, the applicable MCX Gold contract and a retail quote's purity/cost components; no live price is claimed in this Reel.
editorial_brief.boundary: This explains references only; it does not determine a fair jewellery price or predict gold.
editorial_brief.memory_check: Before comparing gold prices, name the reference: global, MCX, or retail.
editorial_brief.human_opening: At a jeweller counter, a family compares the quote in front of them with a different number on a phone.
editorial_brief.primary_source: MCX Gold contract specification plus named global benchmark documentation; retail components must be sourced in the companion carousel.
editorial_brief.save_frame: Before comparing gold: name the reference — global, MCX, or retail.
editorial_brief.voice_tone: Warm, matter-of-fact and slightly protective of the viewer's time; a capable friend explaining a family purchase moment.

voiceover: This quote and the gold price on your phone can differ. Neither is necessarily wrong. Your phone may show global gold in dollars. MCX is a rupee futures contract with an expiry. A jeweller quote includes purity and retail costs. Before comparing gold, name the reference.
caption:
A jeweller quote, MCX Gold and a global gold chart do not all describe the same thing. First identify the reference; then compare the right numbers.

Educational data, not investment advice.
